digest.component_or_area: tracker initialization and environment identity management
propositions: Tracker re-clone mints a new .env-id when git-ignored local state is not carried over, leaving all prior events stamped with an orphaned environment identity
Every op-cert attestation in the store is signed with the writing environment's principal; changing .env-id after attestations were written makes them cryptographically unverifiable
The prior environment's .opcert-key public key is git-ignored and not recoverable from history, so verifying attestations from the old identity is impossible without key publication (out of scope)

Minting .env-id into a store with existing events from another environment must warn loudly on stderr with an explicit override flag, never silently, and must complete to support legitimate multi-clone workflows

rebar fsck must emit a counted ENV_ID_MISMATCH check that fires only when the current environment's own authors also wrote under a different env id, avoiding false positives in healthy multi-clone topologies
